plan.goal: Retrieve UniProt-annotated FASTA sequences for ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase (GO:0034590) and NADPHX epimerase (GO:0034589), profile each set with sequence composition and motif analysis, gather literature evidence for the NAD(P)HX repair system, and produce a ranked list of representative candidates by aggregated biochemical metrics.
assumptions: GO:0034590 and GO:0034589 are assumed to correspond to ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase activity and NADPHX epimerase activity respectively; these IDs must be verified against the current GO release before execution — alternative candidates discussed in literature include GO:0097057 and GO:0097059.

reviewed=true (Swiss-Prot) and exclude_iea=true restrict retrieval to high-confidence, experimentally supported annotations; max_sequences=200 per GO term provides sufficient diversity without exhausting API bandwidth.
No taxon filter is applied so both bacterial (NNRD) and eukaryotic (NAXD/NAXE) orthologs are captured across the full phylogenetic breadth of NAD(P)HX repair.
Ranking is based on sequence composition metrics and annotation quality derived from sequence_analysis; no 3D structure prediction or binding-affinity scoring is applied in this workflow.
pH 7.4 is used as the physiological default for charge-state calculations in sequence_analysis.

Literature search uses a multi-term keyword strategy anchored on NADPHX and repair; low result counts may require a follow-up query with synonyms such as NNRD, NAXD, NAXE, or metabolite damage repair.

esm3 is excluded from this plan because fan-out over representative_sequences requires executor-level foreach and the item schema of representative_sequences is not confirmed at plan time; sequence-composition metrics are sufficient for first-pass candidate ranking.

success_criteria.ranked_output_produced: rank.ranked_candidates contains up to 10 scored entries covering both activity classes
